text: {"facts":[{"statement":"The task is to provide a complete Python 3.11 standard-library program that reads the specified tree input and outputs the minimum vertex-cover cost.","source_ids":["task"]},{"statement":"Costs are nonnegative, n is between 1 and 200000, and a one-vertex tree has minimum cost 0.","source_ids":["task","public1"]},{"statement":"The second public example has minimum cost 5.","source_ids":["public2"]}],"open_requirements":["Produce the complete Python source in the requested code field.","Handle trees up to 200000 vertices within practical time and memory limits.","Ensure the program handles the input and output format exactly."] ,"tentative_options":[{"id":"iterative_tree_dp","method":"Root the tree, build a traversal order iteratively, then compute for each vertex the minimum costs conditional on selecting or not selecting it, using its children’s states.","unverified_assumptions":["The input satisfies the stated tree constraints, so traversal from one root visits every vertex without revisiting vertices other than the parent.","An adjacency-list representation and iterative traversal fit the execution environment’s memory limits."]},{"id":"recursive_tree_dp","method":"Root the tree and compute the same two conditional vertex-cover costs with a recursive depth-first traversal.","unverified_assumptions":["The runtime can safely accommodate recursion depth up to the tree height, or recursion handling can be adjusted without causing resource issues."]}],"possible_checks":["Confirm the output is 0 for the one-vertex public example.","Confirm the output is 5 for the six-vertex public example.","Test boundary shapes such as a long path and a star, and compare small random trees against exhaustive vertex-subset enumeration."]}
